contracts.description: Aborts a [fetchRemote](/wiki/FetchRemote "FetchRemote") or [callRemote](/wiki/CallRemote "CallRemote") request.

parameters.name: theRequest
parameters.description: returned from fetchRemote , callRemote or getRemoteRequests

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns true on success, false when invalid request was provided

contracts.description: This function creates an [[ACL]] entry in the Access Control List system with the specified name.

parameters.name: aclName
parameters.description: The name of the [[ACL]] entry to add.

returns.name: acl object
returns.description: Returns the created [[ACL]] object if successful. Returns **false** if an ACL of the given name could not be created.

contracts.description: This function creates a group in the [[ACL]]. An [[ACL]] group can contain objects like players and resources. They specify who has access to the ACL's in this group.

parameters.name: groupName
parameters.description: The name of the group to create.

returns.name: acl group
returns.description: Returns the created [[aclgroup]] if successful. Returns **false** if failed.

contracts.description: This function destroys the [[ACL]] passed. The destroyed ACL will no longer be valid.

parameters.name: theACL
parameters.description: The ACL to destroy.

returns.name: resullt
returns.description: Returns **true** if successfully destroyed and **false** if it could not be deleted (ie. it's not valid).

contracts.description: This function destroys the given [[ACL]] group. The destroyed ACL group will no longer be valid.

parameters.name: aclGroup
parameters.description: The [[aclgroup]] element to destroy.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the ACL group was successfully deleted, **false** if it could not be deleted for some reason (ie. invalid argument).

contracts.description: Get the [[ACL]] with the given name. If need to get most of the ACL's, you should consider using [[aclList]] to get a table of them all.

parameters.name: aclName
parameters.description: The name to get the ACL belonging to.

returns.name: acl
returns.description: Returns the [[ACL]] with that name if it could be retrieved, **false/nil** if the ACL does not exist or it fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function is used to get the [[ACL]] group with the given name. If you need most of the groups you should consider using [[aclGroupList]] instead to get a [[table]] containing them all.

parameters.name: groupName
parameters.description: The name to get the ACL group from.

returns.name: acl group
returns.description: Returns the [[aclgroup]] if it could be found. Returns **false/nil** if it did not exist or failed for some reason.

contracts.description: Get the name of given [[ACL]].

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to get the name of.

returns.name: acl name
returns.description: Returns the name of the given [[ACL]] as a [[string]] if successful. Returns **false/nil** if unsuccessful, ie the ACL is invalid.

contracts.description: This function returns whether the access for the given right is set to true or false in the [[ACL]].

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to get the right from.

parameters.name: rightName
parameters.description: The right name to return the access value of.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** or **false** if the [[ACL]] gives access or not to the given function. Returns **nil** if it failed for some reason, e.g. an invalid ACL was specified or the right specified does not exist in the ACL.

contracts.description: This function adds the given [[ACL]] to the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). This makes the resources and players in the given ACL group have access to what's specified in the given ACL. The rights for something in the different ACL's in a group are OR-ed together, which means if one ACL gives access to something, this ACL group will have access to that.

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The group to add the [[ACL]] to.

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to add to the group.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the [[ACL]] could be successfully added to the [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup), **false/nil** if either of the elements are invalid, the ACL is already in that group or if something else goes wrong.

contracts.description: This function adds an object to the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). An object can be a player's account, specified as user.. Or a resource, specified as resource.. Objects are specified as strings. The ACL groups work for the user accounts and the resources that are specified in them.

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The group to add the object name string too.

parameters.name: theObject
parameters.description: The object string to add to the given [[ACL]].

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the object was successfully added to the [[ACL]], **false** if it already existed in the list.

contracts.description: This function is used to get the name of the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup).

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The ACL group to get the name of.

returns.name: acl group name
returns.description: Returns the name of the given ACL group as a [[string]] if successful, otherwise **false** or **nil** if the *aclGroup* is invalid or it fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function returns a [[table]] of all the ACL groups.

returns.name: acl groups list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of all the ACL groups if successful, returns an empty [[table]] if no ACL groups exist. **false/nil** can be returned if this function fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function returns a [[table]] over all the ACL's that exist in a given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup).

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup) to get the [[ACL]] elements from.

returns.name: acl's list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of the [[ACL]] elements in the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). This table might be empty. Returns **false** or **nil** if theGroup is invalid or it fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function returns a [[table]] over all the objects that exist in a given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). These are objects like players and resources.

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup) to get the objects from.

returns.name: acl group objects list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of strings in the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). This table might be empty. Returns **false** or **nil** if theGroup is invalid or it fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function removes the given [[ACL]] from the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup).

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The group to remove the given ACL from.

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The ACL to remove from the given group.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the [[ACL]] was successfully removed from the [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup), **false/nil** if it could not be removed for some reason, ie. either of the elements were invalid.

contracts.description: This function removes the given object from the given [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup). The object can be a [[resource]] or a [[player]]. See [[aclGroupAddObject]] for more details.

parameters.name: theGroup
parameters.description: The ACL group to remove the object string from.

parameters.name: theObject
parameters.description: The object to remove from the ACL group.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the object existed in the ACL and could be removed, **false** if it could not be removed for some reason, ie. it did not exist in the given ACL group.

contracts.description: This function returns a list of all the ACLs.

returns.name: acl's list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of all the ACLs. This table can be empty if no ACLs exist. It can also return **false/nil** if it failed for some reason.

contracts.description: This function returns a [[table]] of all the rights that a given [[ACL]] has.

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to get the rights from.

parameters.name: allowedType
parameters.description: The allowed right type. Possible values are general, function, resource and command. If not specified, all types will be retrieved.

returns.name: acl rights list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] over the rights as strings in the given [[ACL]]. This table might be empty. Returns **false** or **nil** if theACL is invalid or it fails for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function returns a [[table]] of all groups the object is in.

parameters.name: theObject
parameters.description: The name of the [[ACL]] entry to get groups of.

returns.name: groups list
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of all groups the object is in on success. This table might be empty. Returns error if something went wrong.

contracts.description: This function reloads the ACL's and the [ACL groups](/reference/aclgroup) from the ACL XML file. All [[ACL]] and [ACL group](/reference/aclgroup) elements are invalid after a call to this and should not be used anymore.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the XML was successfully reloaded from the file, **false** if the XML was invalid, didn't exist or could not be loaded for some other reason.

contracts.description: This function removes the given right (string) from the given [[ACL]].

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to remove the right from.

parameters.name: rightName
parameters.description: The ACL right name to remove.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the given right was successfully removed from the given [[ACL]], **false** or **nil** if it could not be removed for some reason, ie. it didn't exist in the ACL.

contracts.description: The ACL XML file is automatically saved whenever the [[ACL]] is modified, but the automatic save can be delayed by up to 10 seconds for performance reasons. Calling this function will force an immediate save.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the [[ACL]] was successfully changed, **false** if it could not be saved for some reason, ie. file in use.

contracts.description: This functions changes or adds the given right in the given [[ACL]]. The access can be true or false and specifies whether the ACL gives access to the right or not.

parameters.name: theAcl
parameters.description: The [[ACL]] to change the right of.

parameters.name: rightName
parameters.description: The right to add/change the access property of. It must be prefixed with function. or command. or general. or resource..

parameters.name: hasAccess
parameters.description: Whether the access should be set to true or false.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the access was successfully changed, **false** or **nil** if it failed for some reason, ie. invalid ACL or the rightName is invalid.

contracts.description: Acquires one resource-owned reference that keeps a streaming-compatible element present in the local GTA world.

parameters.name: theElement
parameters.description: Streaming-compatible element to retain locally.

contracts.returnDescription: A non-zero resource-private token, or false for an invalid class, missing resource owner, or exhausted script-reference counter.
notes: Independent tokens compose on the same element.
The legacy setElementStreamable boolean owns a separate reference and cannot release this token.
Keeping the native instance alive preserves an already-running GTA task; it does not itself reconstruct work after a syncer change or deliberate release.
contracts.example:
local pedLease = assert(acquireElementStreamingLease(driver))
local vehicleLease = assert(acquireElementStreamingLease(vehicle))

contracts.description: Exclusively loads one GTA mission GXT block for the calling resource.

parameters.name: blockName
parameters.description: Mission GXT block name, limited to GTA's seven-character key format.

contracts.returnDescription: true when acquired or refreshed by the current owner; false when another resource owns the global table or the name is invalid.

contracts.description: Turn a supported object into a real sprayable GTA gang tag. GTA advances the paint progress naturally and the state survives streaming.

parameters.name: theObject
parameters.description: Tag object using model 1490 or 1524 through 1531.

parameters.name: progress
parameters.description: Initial Grove-material progress from 0 through 255.

contracts.returnDescription: true when ownership was acquired or refreshed by the same resource; false for an unsupported object, invalid progress, or another owner.
notes: Ownership and progress survive stream-out and native object recreation.
GTA advances progress in its original 8-alpha spray steps.

contracts.signature: int|false acquirePedNativeCouple(ped a, ped b, int leaderIndex)
contracts.description: Pair two NPCs and GTA makes them walk together, choose their side, hold hands, and look at each other. They separate if they move too far apart.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: First member, simulated by this client.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second member, simulated by this client.

parameters.name: leaderIndex
parameters.description: Which member leads: 1 for a, 2 for b. Any other value is rejected.

contracts.returnDescription: A resource-private couple token, or false when membership, ownership, streaming, or native task construction fails.
notes: The couple is atomic. A half-formed pair is refused instead of partially applied.
Only the current syncer runs the real couple behavior; the token must be reacquired after a handoff.
After the lease exists GTA owns walk-side selection and swapping, hand holding, looking at each other, and abandoning the couple past the give-up distance.

contracts.description: Opens an observer-side presentation channel so a non-syncing client can present two peds as a walking couple.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: First member.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second member.

contracts.returnDescription: A resource-private presentation token, or false when the pair or ownership state is not presentable.
notes: This is appearance only. It runs no couple AI and is the observer counterpart to acquirePedNativeCouple.
A client must not hold a real couple lease and a presentation lease for the same pair.

contracts.description: Exclusively leases one of Neon's stock native-event adapters for a script ped.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Script ped; players are rejected. The mission profile requires setPedMissionActor, while ambient-wander rejects mission actors.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: mission, ambient-wander, or ambient-cop-safe.

contracts.returnDescription: A non-zero resource-private token, or false when the ped, profile prerequisite, profile name, or exclusive ownership check fails.
notes: The logical lease may be acquired before stream-in or sync ownership and survives native recreation and syncer generations.
It becomes active only while this client is the authoritative ped syncer with a live native instance. Another resource cannot lease the same ped on this client.

mission restores the audited mission decision path for events such as an occupied vehicle catching fire. ambient-wander admits stock pedestrian and parked-vehicle avoidance plus civilian gun-threat and damage decisions.

ambient-cop-safe marks the ped as a city cop for locomotion purposes: setPedWander then builds Neon's safe ambient-cop wander task and rejects wanderSensibly = false. It grants no wanted, pursuit, or arrest behavior, which is unreachable by construction rather than suppressed at runtime.
No profile serializes the active response task across migration or loads custom SCM decision-maker files.
contracts.example:
assert(setPedMissionActor(ballas, true))
local token = assert(acquirePedNativeEventProfile(ballas, "mission"))

contracts.description: Put several NPCs into one group so GTA treats them as a single walking group and manages their shared movement.

parameters.name: peds
parameters.description: Array of two to five script peds simulated by this client.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Currently ambient-random.

contracts.returnDescription: A resource-private group token, or false when membership, ownership, streaming, or native group-slot checks fail.
notes: The token is resource-owned and must be reacquired after a syncer handoff.
Only the current owner runs the native group intelligence.

contracts.description: Acquires the resource-exclusive GTA script camera and returns a generation token.

parameters.name: inhibitControls
parameters.description: Also engage the reference-counted gameplay inhibitor and native player-safe braking bit.

contracts.returnDescription: A non-zero generation token, or false when another resource owns the lease.
contracts.example:
local token = assert(acquireScriptCamera(true))
assert(setScriptCameraFixed(token, Vector3(0, 0, 20), Vector3(0, 0, 0)))

contracts.description: This function adds an [[account]] to the list of registered accounts of the current server.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the [account](account) you wish to make, this normally is the player's name.

parameters.name: pass
parameters.description: The password to set for this [account](account) for future logins.

parameters.name: allowCaseVariations
parameters.description: Whether the username is case sensitive (if this is set to true, usernames "Bob" and "bob" will refer to different accounts).

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns an [[account]] or **false** if the account already exists or an error occured.

contracts.description: This function will add a [[ban]] for the specified IP/username/serial to the server.

parameters.name: IP
parameters.description: The IP to be banned. If you don't want to ban by IP, set this to [[nil]].

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The username (nick) to be banned. If you don't want to ban by username, set this to [[nil]].

parameters.name: serial
parameters.description: The [[serial]] to be banned. If you don't want to ban by serial, set this to [[nil]].

parameters.name: responsibleElement
parameters.description: The element that is responsible for banning the IP/username/serial. This can be a [[player]] or the [[root]]. This also can be a [[string]] - max 30 characters.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: The reason the IP/username/serial will be banned from the server. Max 125 characters.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: The amount of seconds the player will be banned from the server for. This can be 0 for an infinite amount of time.

returns.name: ban
returns.description: Returns the new [[ban]] if the IP/username/serial was banned successfully, **false** if invalid arguments are specified.

contracts.signature: ban|false addBan([string IP = '', string Username = '', string Serial = '', player|string responsible = 'Console', string reason = '', int|string seconds = 0, string neonAccountId = '', string discordId = ''])
contracts.description: Extends MTA's existing ban constructor with optional verified Neon and Discord identity fields.

parameters.name: IP
parameters.description: Optional IP address.

parameters.name: Username
parameters.description: Optional account username.

parameters.name: Serial
parameters.description: Optional MTA serial.

parameters.name: responsible
parameters.description: Responsible player or display name.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Ban reason.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: Duration in seconds; 0 is permanent.

parameters.name: neonAccountId
parameters.description: Canonical lowercase Neon account UUID.

parameters.name: discordId
parameters.description: Discord snowflake containing 17 through 20 decimal digits.

contracts.returnDescription: The created ban, or false when validation fails, no usable identifier is supplied, or any supplied identifier overlaps an existing ban.
notes: Neon rejects an overlapping identifier instead of silently merging bans.
A live serial ban captures that player's verified identities automatically. An offline serial-only call cannot infer them.
Identity enforcement only applies when a later connection supplies a verified identity; neon_auth=required provides the strongest coverage.

contracts.description: This function allows tracing of MTA functions and events. It should only be used when debugging scripts as it may degrade script performance.

parameters.name: hookType
parameters.description: The type of hook to add. This can be: preEvent postEvent preFunction postFunction preEventFunction postEventFunction

parameters.name: callbackFunction
parameters.description: The function to call Returning the string "skip" from the callback function will cause the original function/event to be skipped

parameters.name: nameList
parameters.description: Table of strings for restricting which functions and events the hook will be triggered on addDebugHook and removeDebugHook will only be hooked if they are specified in the name list

returns.name: value

contracts.description: This function subscribes a [[player]] to specific [element data](/reference/Element_data). This function is used together with [[setElementData]] in `"subscribe"` mode.

parameters.name: theElement
parameters.description: The element you wish to subscribe the player to.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key you wish to subscribe the player to.

parameters.name: thePlayer
parameters.description: The player you wish to subscribe.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the player was subscribed, **false** otherwise.

contracts.description: This function allows you to register a custom [event](/reference/Event_System "Event"). Custom events function exactly like the built\-in events. See [event system](/reference/Event_System "Event system") for more information on the event system.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event you wish to create.

parameters.name: allowRemoteTrigger
parameters.description: A boolean specifying whether this event can be called remotely using [[triggerClientEvent]] / [[triggerServerEvent]] or not.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the event was added successfully, otherwise **false** if the event already exists **built-in game events** or if it fails for any other reason.

contracts.description: This function will add an [event](/reference/Event_System "Event System") handler. An event handler is a function that will be called when the event it's attached to is triggered. See [event system](/reference/Event_System "Event System") for more information on how the event system works.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the [event](/reference/Event_System "Event System") you want to attach the handler function to. **Note: The maximum allowed length is 100 ASCII characters (that is, English letters and numerals)**

parameters.name: attachedTo
parameters.description: The [[element]] you wish to attach the handler to. The handler will only be called when the event it is attached to is triggered for this element, or one of its children. Often, this can be the root element (meaning the handler will be called when the event is triggered for *any* element).

parameters.name: handlerFunction()
parameters.description: The handler function you wish to call when the event is triggered. This function will be passed all of the event's parameters as arguments, but it isn't required that it takes all of them.

parameters.name: propagate
parameters.description: A boolean representing whether the handler will be triggered if the event was propagated down or up the [element tree](/reference/Element_tree "Element tree") (starting from the source), and not triggered directly on attachedTo (that is, handlers attached with this argument set to false will only be triggered if source == this ). In GUI events you will probably want to set this to false .

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: A string representing the trigger order priority relative to other event handlers of the same name. Possible values are:

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the event handler was attached successfully. otherwise **false** if the specified event could not be found or any parameters were invalid.

contracts.signature: bool addModel2DFX(int model, float x, float y, float z, string type, table properties)
contracts.description: Adds a resource-owned 2DFX effect to a GTA model.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model ID from 0 through 65535.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Effect X, local to the model.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Effect Y, local to the model.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Effect Z, local to the model.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: light, particle, roadsign, escalator or sun_glare.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: Property table for that type. light requires all fifteen fields; sun_glare takes none.

contracts.returnDescription: true when the effect was added; false for an invalid model, position, type or property table.
notes: The effect belongs to the model, not to a placed object, so every instance of that model gets it.
Already-streamed instances need a restream before the change is visible.
The effect is owned by the calling resource and removed when that resource stops.
contracts.example: addModel2DFX(1337, 0, 0, 1.2, "particle", { name = "smoke_flare" })

contracts.description: This function is used to set the current clothes on a [ped](/wiki/Ped "Ped").

parameters.name: clothesTexture
parameters.description: A string determining the clothes texture that will be added. See the clothes catalog .

parameters.name: clothesModel
parameters.description: A string determining the clothes model that will be added. See the clothes catalog .

parameters.name: clothesType
parameters.description: A integer representing the clothes slot/type the clothes should be added to. See the clothes catalog .

returns.name: value
returns.description: This function returns true if the clothes were successfully added to the ped, false otherwise.

contracts.signature: bool addPedNativeBikeJackTask(player victim, ped jacker, vehicle bike, int door, int draggedPedDownTime, bool victimIsDriver, int token)
contracts.description: Installs GTA's canonical bike-jacked task on the authoritative local player after a synchronized ambient gang carjack is validated.

parameters.name: victim
parameters.description: Local player currently occupying the target bike.

parameters.name: jacker
parameters.description: Ambient script ped that owns the validated native event profile.

parameters.name: bike
parameters.description: Bike, BMX, or quadbike being jacked.

parameters.name: door
parameters.description: Canonical native bike door index 10 or 11.

parameters.name: draggedPedDownTime
parameters.description: Canonical task value: 0 for the driver or 200 for the passenger path.

parameters.name: victimIsDriver
parameters.description: Whether the local victim occupies the driver seat.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Native event-profile lease token for the jacker.

contracts.returnDescription: true when the owner-authorized native task was queued on the local victim; false when seat, vehicle, token, or task validation fails.
notes: This is the low-level victim-side bridge used by synchronized ambient carjacks; ordinary gameplay resources normally use the higher-level population runtime instead.

contracts.signature: bool addPedNativeDamageResponseEvent(ped thePed, ped attacker, int weapon, int bodypart, int token)
contracts.description: Replays GTA's civilian damage decision on the authoritative owner without applying physical damage again.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Living script ped that owns the active ambient-wander profile on this client.

parameters.name: attacker
parameters.description: Different streamed ped or player responsible for the already synchronized hit.

parameters.name: weapon
parameters.description: MTA weapon ID from unarmed through fall.

parameters.name: bodypart
parameters.description: 0 for unknown, or an MTA body-part ID from torso through head.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Resource-private ambient-wander token for the target ped.

contracts.returnDescription: true when GTA accepted the behavior-only event; false for invalid arguments, a stale or foreign token, an observer client, a dead or unstreamed target, or a missing native attacker.
notes: Call this only after MTA has synchronized the real hit and only when the owner's ordinary native damage event was absent.
The replay carries no physical damage, so it can select a stock fall, recovery, flee, cower, or fight response without reducing health twice.

contracts.signature: bool addPedNativeGunAimedAtEvent(ped thePed, ped aimingPed, int token)
contracts.description: Inserts GTA's real aimed-at event on the authoritative ambient-ped owner.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Living script ped that owns the active ambient-wander profile on this client.

parameters.name: aimingPed
parameters.description: Different streamed ped or player whose synchronized aim triggered the event.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Resource-private ambient-wander token for the target ped.

contracts.returnDescription: true when GTA accepted the event; false for an invalid or identical ped, a stale or foreign token, an observer client, a dead or unstreamed target, or a missing native aiming ped.
notes: The server should validate the synchronized aim transition before asking the current owner to call this bridge.
The event lets the civilian decision maker choose its stock response. It does not grant authority to an observer or advance mission state.

contracts.description:
This functions performs an arithmetic shift on the integer **value** by integer **n** positions. In an *arithmetic shift*, zeros are shifted in to replace the discarded bits. In a *right arithmetic* shift, the [sign bit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sign_bit) is shifted in on the left, thus preserving the sign of the operand.
See [Bitwise operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitwise_operation#Arithmetic_shift) for more details.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value you want to perform the arithmetic shift on.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The amount of positions to shift the value by.

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns the arithmetic shifted value as integer .

contracts.description: This function allows you to call functions that have been exported with HTTP access by other MTA servers. The calls are asynchronous so you do not get an immediate result from the call, instead a callback function you specify is called when the call returns.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: This is a host name - including the HTTP port - of the server you wish to connect to.

parameters.name: queueName
parameters.description: MISSING_PARAM_DESC

parameters.name: connectionAttempts
parameters.description: Number of times to retry if the remote host does not respond. In the case of a non-responding remote server, each connection attempt will timeout after 6 seconds. Therefore, the default setting of 10 connection attempts means it will be 60 seconds before your script gets a callback about the error. Reducing this value to 2 for example, will decrease that period to 12 seconds

parameters.name: connectTimeout
parameters.description: Number of milliseconds each connection attempt will take before timing out

parameters.name: resourceName
parameters.description: This is a name of the resource that contains the exported function you want to call.

parameters.name: functionName
parameters.description: This is a string with the name of the function which you want to call.

parameters.name: callbackFunction
parameters.description: This is the function that should receive the data returned from the remote function call. The argument list should match the format of the data returned. The callback function will be passed a string containing "ERROR" followed by an integer indicating the error code when an error occurs calling the function. A list of error codes can be found here .

parameters.name: arguments...
parameters.description: MISSING_PARAM_DESC

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns true if the function has been called, false otherwise.

contracts.signature: fire|bool createFire(float x, float y, float z [, table options])
contracts.description: Creates a managed fire element when given an options table, or the original native GTA fire otherwise.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: World X.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: World Y.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: World Z.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional table of duration, strength, damage, damageTargets, spread, maxGenerations, source and target. Passing it is what makes the fire managed.

contracts.returnDescription: A fire element for the managed form; a boolean for the legacy native form; false on failure.
notes: Passing a table as the fourth argument is the switch: it returns a real element with a persistent identity that can be changed while it burns.
On the client, a number or omitted fourth argument keeps the original native GTA fire and still returns a boolean, so existing resources are unaffected.
On the server, a number fourth argument is read as strength and still creates a managed fire.
Defaults are duration 5000 ms, strength 1.0, damage on, spread off, maxGenerations 0, and all four damage targets enabled.
Server-created fires are synchronized to every client, and a player joining mid-burn receives the remaining lifetime rather than a restarted one.

contracts.description: This function opens a connection to a database and returns an element that can be used with [[dbQuery]] and other db functions. To disconnect use [[destroyElement]].

parameters.name: databaseType
parameters.description: The type of database. This can be either **sqlite** or **mysql**.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description:
The target to connect to. The format of this depends on the database type.

- For SQLite it is a [[filepath]] to a SQLite database file. If the filepath starts with ":/" then the server's global databases directory is used. The file will be created if it does not exist.
- For MySQL it is a list of key=value pairs separated by semicolons. Supported keys are:
  - **dbname**: Name of the database to use e.g. dbname=test
  - **host**: Host address e.g. host=127.0.0.1
  - **port**: Host port e.g. port=3306 (optional, defaults to standard MySQL port if not used).
  - **unix_socket**: Unix socket or named pipe to use (optional).
  - **charset**: Communicate with the server using a character which is different from the default e.g. charset=utf8 (optional).

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Usually required for MySQL, ignored by SQLite

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Usually required for MySQL, ignored by SQLite

parameters.name: options
parameters.description:
List of key=value pairs separated by semicolons. Supported keys are:

- **share**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default value for SQLite is "share=1", for MySQL is "share=0"). When set to 1, the connection is shared and will be used by other calls to dbConnect with the same host string. This is usually a good thing for SQLite connections, but not so good for MySQL unless care is taken.
- **batch**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default is "batch=1"). When set to 1, queries called in the same frame are automatically batched together which can significantly speed up inserts/updates. The downside is you lose control of the feature that is used to achieve batching (For SQLite it is transactions, for MySQL it is autocommit mode). Therefore, if you use transactions, lock tables or control autocommit yourself, you may want to disable this feature.
- **autoreconnect**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default value "autoreconnect=1"). When set to 1, dropped connections will automatically be reconnected. Note that session variables (incl. SET NAMES), user variables, table locks and temporary tables will be reset because of the reconnection. So if you use these fancy features, you will need to turn autoreconnect off and cope with dropped connections some other way.
- **log**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default value "log=1"). When set to 0, activity from this connection will not be recorded in the [database debug log file](/articles/Server_Commands#debugdb).
- **tag**: (Default value "tag=script"). A string which helps identify activity from this connection in the [database debug log file](/articles/Server_Commands#debugdb).
- **suppress**: A comma separated list of error codes to ignore. (eg. "suppress=1062,1169").
- **multi_statements**: Enable multiple statements (separated by a semi-colon) in one query. Use [[dbPrepareString]] when building a multiple statement query to reduce SQL injection risks.
- **queue**: Name of the queue to use. (Default value for SQLite is "sqlite", for MySQL default is the host string from the host argument). Asynchronous database queries in the same queue are processed in order, one at a time. Any name can be used.
- **use_ssl**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default value is 0), ignored by SQLite.
- **get_server_public_key**: which can be set to 0 or 1. (Default value is 1), ignored by SQLite. When set to 1, this enables the client to request from the server the public key required for RSA key pair-based password exchange. This option applies to clients that authenticate with the `caching_sha2_password`` authentication plugin.

returns.name: db connection handle
returns.description: Returns a [database connection](/reference/db-connection) element unless there are problems, in which case it return **false**.

contracts.description: This function executes a database query using the supplied connection. No query result is returned.

parameters.name: databaseConnection
parameters.description: A database connection element previously returned from [[dbConnect]].

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: An SQL query. Positions where parameter values will be inserted are marked with a `?`.

parameters.name: param1 [, var param2 ...]
parameters.description:
A variable number of parameters. These must be strings or numbers - it is important to make sure they are of the correct type. Also, the number of parameters passed must be equal to the number of `?` characters in the query string.

String parameters are automatically quoted and escaped as required. (If you do not want a string quoted, use `??`). Make sure that numbers are in number format as a string number is treated differently.

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns **true** unless the connection is incorrect, in which case it returns **false**.

contracts.description: This function checks the progress of a database query.

parameters.name: queryHandle
parameters.description: A [query handle](/reference/db-query) previously returned from [[dbQuery]].

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: How many milliseconds to wait for a result. Use 0 for an instant response (which may return [[nil]]). Use -1 to wait until a result is ready. Note: A wait here will freeze the entire server just like [[executeSQLQuery]].

parameters.name: multipleResults
parameters.description: Set to *true* to enable the return values from multiple queries.

returns.name: result
returns.description:
Returns [[nil]] if the query results are not yet ready. You should try again in a little while. (If you give up waiting for a result, be sure to call [[dbFree]]). Returns **false** if the query string contained an error, the connection has been lost or the query handle is incorrect. This automatically frees the query handle, so you do not have to call [[dbFree]]. This also returns two extra values: error code and error message. Returns a [[table]] with the result of the query when the query has successfully completed. This automatically frees the query handle, so you do not have to call [[dbFree]]. If **multipleResults** is set to *true*, it will first return a table pertaining to one query, followed by the results for that query and so on for the next queries. This also returns extra values: number of affected rows and last insert id.
The table is of the format
{ { colname1=value1, colname2=value2, ... }, { colname1=value3, colname2=value4, ... }, ... }

contracts.description: This function creates a [[shader]] element that can be used in the dxDraw functions. Successful shader creation is not guaranteed unless the [Effect File](/articles/shaders) contains a fallback technique which will work on every existing PC.

parameters.name: filepath/raw_data
parameters.description: The [filepath](/reference/Filepath) of the shader [Effect File (.fx)](/reference/Shaders) file or whole data buffer of the shader file.

parameters.name: macros
parameters.description: A [[table]] contains macros in an ordered and/or unordered way. See example below.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: If more than one shader is matched to a world texture, the shader with the highest priority will be used. If there is more than one shader with the same highest priority, the most recently created shader is used.

parameters.name: maxDistance
parameters.description: If non-zero, the shader will be applied to textures nearer than maxDistance only. This can speed up rendering, but (to look good) may require the shader to fade out it's own effect as the texture reaches maxDistance.

parameters.name: layered
parameters.description: When set to true, the shader will be drawn in a separate render pass. Several layered shaders can be drawn on the same world texture. (To avoid [Z fighting](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z-fighting) artifacts, you may have to add `DepthBias=-0.0002;` to the technique pass, but this might cause visual artifacts when applied on vehicles).

parameters.name: elementTypes
parameters.description: A comma seperated list of element types to restrict this shader to. Valid element types are: - **world** - Textures in the GTA world - **ped** - Player and ped textures - **vehicle** - Vehicles textures - **object** - Objects textures other - **other** - Element textures which are not peds, vehicles or objects - **all** - Everything

returns.name: shader element
returns.description: Returns a [[shader]] element and the name of the technique that will be used if successful, **false** if invalid arguments were passed to the function or there is insufficient resources available.

returns.name: technique
returns.description: Returns a [[shader]] element and the name of the technique that will be used if successful, **false** if invalid arguments were passed to the function or there is insufficient resources available.

contracts.description: This function retrieves the width and height (in pixels) of a certain piece of text, if it were to be drawn using [[dxDrawText]].

parameters.description: A string representing the text for which you wish to retrieve with width for.

parameters.name: scaleY

returns.name: height

contracts.description:
This function allows for the positioning of dxDraw calls to be automatically adjusted according to the client's aspect ratio setting. This lasts for a single execution of an event handler for one of the following events: [[onClientRender]], [[onClientPreRender]] and [[onClientHUDRender]]. So the function has to be called every frame, just like dxDraws.

This is particularly useful for draws that must align with the GTA HUD, for which the sizing and positioning can vary for different aspect ratios.

parameters.name: bEnabled
parameters.description: Should the adjustment be enabled or disabled.

parameters.name: sourceRatio
parameters.description: This should be set to the aspect ratio the dxDraws were originally designed in.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** when it was changed successfully, or **false** otherwise.

contracts.description: This function sets the current blend mode for the dxDraw functions. Changing the blend mode can increase the quality when drawing text or certain other images to a render target. As a general guide use **modulate\_add** when drawing text to a render target, and **add** when drawing the render target to the screen. Don't forget to restore the default **blend** at the end \- See the example below.

parameters.name: blendMode
parameters.description: The blend mode to use.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if successful, or **false** if invalid arguments were passed to the function.

contracts.description: This function sets the amount of geometric sub-division to use when drawing a [[shader]] element with [[dxDrawImage]]. Using tessellation allows a shader to manipulate the shape of the rendered image at each sub-division boundary.

returns.name: result

contracts.description: This function applies a 3D transformation to a [[shader]] element when it is drawn with [[dxDrawImage]].

parameters.description: The [[shader]] element whose transformation is to be changed.

parameters.name: rotationX
parameters.description: Rotation angle in degrees around the X axis (Left,right). This will make the shader rotate along its width.

parameters.name: rotationY
parameters.description: Rotation angle in degrees around the Y axis (Up,down). This will make the shader rotate along its height.

parameters.name: rotationZ
parameters.description: Rotation angle in degrees around the Z axis (In,out). This will make the shader rotate in a similar way to the rotation argument in [[dxDrawImage]].

parameters.name: rotationCenterOffsetX
parameters.description: The center of rotation offset X position in screen relative units.

parameters.name: rotationCenterOffsetY
parameters.description: The center of rotation offset Y position in screen relative units.

parameters.name: rotationCenterOffsetZ
parameters.description: The center of rotation offset Z position in screen relative units.

parameters.name: bRotationCenterOffsetOriginIsScreen
parameters.description: Set to true if the center of rotation origin should be the center of the screen rather than the center of the image.

parameters.name: perspectiveCenterOffsetX
parameters.description: The center of perspective offset X position in screen relative units.

parameters.name: perspectiveCenterOffsetY
parameters.description: The center of perspective offset Y position in screen relative units.

parameters.name: bPerspectiveCenterOffsetOriginIsScreen
parameters.description: Set to true if the center of perspective origin should be the center of the screen rather than the center of the image.

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns **true** if the shader element's transform was successfully changed, **false** otherwise.

contracts.description:
This function enables or disables asynchronous model loading. Enabling
asynchronous model loading may reduce the small pauses that occur when a new model
is displayed for the first time. However, it can cause the new models to appear
slightly later than they might have otherwise.

If asynchronous loading is disabled, MTA requests all resources to be loaded at the time they have been requested. This will halt game execution for the time being.
Otherwise, all resource requests are queued up on the to-be-loaded queue. At the beginning of the game frame, the GTA:SA streaming system is updated, along with its streaming slicers. This is when a model is loaded after going through multiple stages. Having asynchronous loading disabled forces all stages to be consecutively run through.

For more details read [GTA:SA Resource Streaming](/reference/GTA_Resource_Streaming).

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: Set to **true/false** to enable/disable asynchronous loading.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: If set to **true**, ignores the client's preferences.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the function executed successfully, **false** otherwise.

contracts.returnDescription: true when the new collision was built and applied; false when the element has no loaded collision or the rebuild failed.
notes: This is the reason to generate collision rather than ship a .col: the new shape lands immediately on objects that are already streamed in.
Rebuild only when the shape actually changes. Keep a signature of the current dimensions and skip identical frames when the shape is driven by held keys or continuous input.
The previous collision model is destroyed after the replacement succeeds.

contracts.description: This function allows you to post and receive data from HTTP servers. The calls are asynchronous so you do not get an immediate result from the call, instead a callback function you specify is called when the download completes.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: A table containing any request options: queueName: Name of the queue to use. Any name can be used. If not set, the queue name is "default". Requests in the same queue are processed in order, one at a time. connectionAttempts: Number of times to retry if the remote host does not respond. (Defaults to 10) connectTimeout: Number of milliseconds each connection attempt will take before timing out. (Defaults to 10000) postData: A string specifying any data you want to send to the remote HTTP server. postIsBinary : A boolean specifying if the data is text, or binary. (Defaults to false) method: A string specifying the request method. (Defaults to GET or POST) headers: A table containing HTTP request headers. e.g.{ Pragma="no-cache" } maxRedirects: An integer limiting the number of HTTP redirections to automatically follow. (Defaults to 8) username: A string specifying the username for protected pages. password: A string specifying the password for protected pages. formFields: A table containing form items to submit. (for POST method only) e.g.{ name="bob", email=" [email protected] " }

parameters.name: callbackFunction
parameters.description: This is the function that should receive the data returned from the remote server. The callback argument list should be: responseData - A string containing the remote response responseInfo - A table containing: success - A boolean indicating if the request was successful. statusCode - An integer status/error code. See the list of possible error values below. headers - A table containing the HTTP response headers arguments... - The arguments that were passed into fetchRemote

parameters.name: callbackArguments
parameters.description: A table containing arguments you may want to pass to the callback.

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns a request value which can be used with getRemoteRequestInfo or abortRemoteRequest

contracts.signature: table|false, string? getAmbientPedGangGroupCandidate(Vector3 origin, int gangId [, int maxMembers = 4])
contracts.description: Asks GTA for a native ambient gang-group placement with two to four proposed members.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Finite population origin.

parameters.name: gangId
parameters.description: Supported native gang ID from 0 through 7.

parameters.name: maxMembers
parameters.description: Maximum proposed group size from 2 through 4.

contracts.returnDescription: An array of member candidates with model, pedType, position, heading and gang metadata; or false plus a bounded miss reason.
notes: This is a placement oracle only. The server must validate and create the real group elements.

contracts.description: Returns GTA's current ambient population targets, zone state, density multipliers, and gang weights.
contracts.returnDescription: A table containing civilian, cop, gang and dealer targets, supportedTarget, density and creation-distance fields, zone metadata, worldLevel, copSuppressionFlags, zoneLabel, and ten gang weights; false when the native population state is not active.
notes: The profile is read-only. A server still decides how many shared MTA peds to create.
dealerTarget is part of the current native popcycle calculation even though dealers are not counted as ordinary GTA total-ped occupancy.
rawCopTarget keeps the unmodified popcycle result while copTarget applies the normal ambient-cop guards.
copSuppressionFlags is a bitfield naming which guard reduced the cop target: 1 zone no-cops, 2 random cops disabled, 4 gang war being fought, 8 high altitude.
worldLevel and zoneLabel identify the native world level and navigation zone the profile was computed for.

contracts.signature: table|false, string? getAmbientPedSpawnCandidate(Vector3 origin [, string selection = "auto", int gangId = -1])
contracts.description: Ask GTA where it would naturally place an NPC near a position. The result includes the suggested skin, NPC type, position, and facing direction—without creating the NPC.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Finite population origin.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: auto, civilian, gang, dealer, or cop.

parameters.name: gangId
parameters.description: Required only for gang selection; supported native gang IDs are 0 through 7.

contracts.returnDescription: A candidate table with model, pedType, position, direction, pathLerp, populationClass, worldLevel, and gang; or false plus a bounded miss reason.
notes: The function creates no ped and grants no authority.
Forced gang, dealer, or cop queries do not silently fall back to civilians.
populationClass reports civilian, gang, dealer, or cop for the returned candidate.
contracts.example:
local candidate = getAmbientPedSpawnCandidate(localPlayer.position, "dealer")
if candidate then
    outputDebugString(("dealer model: %d"):format(candidate.model))
end

contracts.description: Ask GTA which civilian road vehicle naturally fits the current area and population settings—without creating it.
contracts.returnDescription: A table with model, carGroup, and vehicleClass; or false plus a reason when GTA cannot select a road vehicle.
notes: The choice comes from GTA's current population and car-group state.
The server still decides whether to accept the proposal and create the vehicle.

contracts.description: Ask GTA which pedestrian skins naturally fit a vehicle, so it can be created with a suitable driver and passengers.

parameters.name: vehicleModelId
parameters.description: Supported civilian road-vehicle model ID.

parameters.name: maximumOccupants
parameters.description: Maximum number of proposed occupants, from 1 through 4.

contracts.returnDescription: An array of one to four pedestrian model IDs, or false when GTA cannot produce a compatible occupant list.
notes: The first model is used for the driver; any remaining models can be used for passengers.
The function creates no peds or vehicle.

contracts.signature: table|false, string? getAmbientVehicleSpawnCandidate(Vector3 origin, int modelId)
contracts.description: Ask GTA to choose a valid road lane, position, direction, speed, and driving style for a vehicle near the player—without creating the vehicle.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Position around which GTA should look for a road.

parameters.name: modelId
parameters.description: Supported civilian road-vehicle model ID.

contracts.returnDescription: A table with model, x, y, z, rotation, cruiseSpeed, vehicleClass, and drivingStyle; or false plus a reason when GTA cannot find a valid road placement.
notes: The function only proposes a spawn. The server still creates and owns the real vehicle.
The result uses GTA's road network and lane placement, including a ground check.
contracts.example:
local model = getAmbientVehicleModelCandidate()
if model then
    local spawn = getAmbientVehicleSpawnCandidate(localPlayer.position, model.model)
    if spawn then
        outputDebugString(("vehicle %d at %.1f, %.1f"):format(spawn.model, spawn.x, spawn.y))
    end
end

contracts.description: This function gets the fast fourier transform data for an audio stream which is a table of floats representing the current audio frame. This allows things like visualisations. A fast fourier transform generates a table of all the frequencies of the current audio frame which starts at the bass end of the spectrum to mids to highs in that order. Should you have any problems there is an example resource located on the resources repository: [Visualiser](https://github.com/multitheftauto/mtasa-resources/tree/master/%5Bgameplay%5D/visualiser). Just type startmusic mystreamurl in your console and it will play on the cinema billboard near A51. If the element is a player, this function will use the players voice.

parameters.name: theSound
parameters.description: A [[sound]] element that is created using [[playSound]] or [[playSound3D]]. Streams are also supported.

parameters.name: bands
parameters.description: Post processing option allows you to split the samples into the desired amount of bands or bars so if you only need 5 bars this saves a lot of cpu power compared to trying to do it in Lua.

returns.name: fft-data
returns.description: Returns a [[table]] of samples/2 (or bands if bands is used) floats representing the current audio frame. Returns **false** if the sound is not playing yet or hasn't buffered in the case of streams.

contracts.description:
This function returns whether or not the given object has access to perform the given action.

Scripts frequently wish to limit access to features to particular users. The naïve way to do this would be to check if the player who is attempting to perform an action is in a particular group (usually the Admin group). The main issue with doing this is that the Admin group is not guaranteed to exist. It also doesn't give the server admin any flexibility. He might want to allow his 'moderators' access to the function you're limiting access to, or he may want it disabled entirely.

parameters.name: theObject
parameters.description: The object to test if has permission to. This can be a client element (ie. a [[player]]), a [[resource]] or a [[string]] in the form user.name or resource.name.

parameters.name: theRight
parameters.description: The action to test if the given object has access to. Ie. function.kickPlayer.

parameters.name: defaultPermission
parameters.description: The default permission if none is specified in either of the groups the given object is a member of. If this is left to true, the given object will have permissions to perform the action unless the opposite is explicitly specified in the [[ACL]]. If false, the action will be denied by default unless explicitly approved by the [Access Control List](Access_Control_List).

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the given object has permission to perform the given action, **false** otherwise. Returns **nil** if the function failed because of bad arguments.

contracts.description:
This function makes the user's browser show a 'basic authentication' login box.
The result of the login is handled automatically by the server.
If the user has not logged in satisfactorily, you should just call the **httpRequestLogin** function again.
It is the script's responsibility to judge when the user is logged in satisfactorily - you can use the [user](/reference/Predefined_variables.html#http) variable can be used to check if the user has logged in with an account you are happy with.
If the logged in user doesn't meet whatever criteria you have, you can just call **httpRequestLogin** again and they will be re-promoted for their password.

This function works by setting a header `('Authentication')` and a return code `(403 - Authentication required)`. As such, nothing happens until you finish the page. The content of the page is generally not displayed unless the login fails.

contracts.description: Opts an MTA object into GTA's own rigid-body physics, or back out of it.

parameters.description: Object created with createObject.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether the object is simulated by GTA physics.

contracts.returnDescription: true when the state was applied; false for an invalid object.
notes: Once enabled, setElementVelocity and setElementAngularVelocity set real motion instead of being overwritten on the next sync tick.
The syncer sends position, rotation, linear velocity and angular velocity, so a rolling or spinning object keeps its motion through a syncer change.
This does not generate collision. The object is simulated with whatever collision its model already has, so a model without useful collision will not behave.
There is no separate tuning API: a physical object uses GTA's own object properties, so mass, turn mass, air resistance and elasticity come from setObjectProperty.
contracts.example:

setElementAngularVelocity(ball, 0, 0.4, 0)

contracts.description: Give an NPC driver a destination and GTA's original driving AI takes over: it follows the native road network, chooses a route, steers, accelerates, and brakes as it drives toward the target.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Living streamed ped simulated by this client.

parameters.name: theVehicle
parameters.description: Streamed, non-blown vehicle occupied by the ped in driver seat 0 and controlled by this client.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Finite world destination.

parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: Finite cruise speed from 0 up to, but not including, 255.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Integer 0..3 or normal, accurate, straight_line, or racing.

parameters.name: drivingStyle
parameters.description: Integer 0..6 or one of the documented stop/avoid/plough-through names.

contracts.returnDescription: true when GTA accepted the scripted command; false when ped, vehicle, seat, ownership, target, speed, mode, style, or task construction is invalid.
notes: true does not mean the destination has been reached; the API has no completion event or durable task handle.
The linked route harness exercises this task inside a native sequence. The standalone call has not been exercised separately in game.
contracts.example:
-- client.lua
-- The driver uses GTA's road AI to reach the destination.
local car = createVehicle(492, 2494.0, -1684.0, 13.4)
local driver = createPed(105, 2494.0, -1684.0, 13.4)
local destination = Vector3(2365.0, -1665.0, 13.4)

if car and driver then
    warpPedIntoVehicle(driver, car, 0)
    assert(setPedDriveTo(driver, car, destination, 18.0, "normal", "avoid_cars"))
end

contracts.signature: bool setPedTaskSequence(ped thePed, table tasks [, bool repeat = false])
contracts.description: Give an NPC up to eight actions—walk, drive, shoot, flee, leave a vehicle, or die—and GTA performs them in order or repeats the sequence.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Living streamed ped simulated by this client.

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: Array of 1–8 leave_car, leave_car_immediately, go_to, shoot_at, drive_to, smart_flee, or die descriptors.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: Repeat the native sequence after its final child.

contracts.returnDescription: true when GTA accepted the composed sequence; false after validation, factory, sequence-slot, or dispatch failure.
notes: leave_car requires a vehicle; go_to and shoot_at use the same fields and defaults as their standalone functions.

drive_to requires x/y/z and speed, with optional mode, drivingStyle, and vehicleModel. It carries no vehicle pointer, matching SCM's placeholders so GTA binds the ped's current vehicle when that child starts.
leave_car_immediately requires a streamed vehicle. smart_flee requires a streamed target ped, a positive safeDistance, and a duration of -1 or at least zero. die has no extra fields.
Child-task ownership transfers into GTA's global sequence template; the Lua table is not retained.

contracts.signature: bool setPedWander(ped thePed [, string movement = "walk", int direction = -1, bool wanderSensibly = true])
contracts.description: Tell an NPC to wander and GTA's original pedestrian AI takes over: it follows the native path network, chooses its own direction from node to node, and keeps walking or running without Lua waypoints.

parameters.name: thePed
parameters.description: Living streamed ped simulated by this client.

parameters.name: movement
parameters.description: walk or run.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: -1 for GTA's native random direction, or a direction from 0 through 7.

parameters.name: wanderSensibly
parameters.description: Use the native sensible-wander behavior. Rejected as false while the ambient-cop-safe profile is selected.

contracts.returnDescription: true when the task was queued; false for invalid movement, direction, ped state, ownership, or task construction.
notes: A ped holding the ambient-cop-safe event profile gets Neon's safe ambient-cop wander task instead of WanderStandard.
Under that profile wanderSensibly = false returns false rather than being applied. Retail WanderCop hardcodes sensible walking, so accepting it would produce a hybrid state neither task can reach.
contracts.example:
-- client.lua
-- This local ped picks its own walking path instead of following Lua waypoints.
local pedestrian = createPed(7, 2498.0, -1687.0, 13.5)

if pedestrian then
    assert(setPedWander(pedestrian, "walk", -1, true))
end

contracts.description: A [text display](/wiki/Textdisplay "Textdisplay") is like a canvas that can contain many [items of text](/wiki/Textitem "Textitem"). Each display can be seen by multiple observers (players) and each player can see multiple displays.

This function creates a text item. A text item represents a single area of text, much like a label does in standard GUI programming. A text item can only be seen by players if it is added to a [textdisplay](/wiki/Textdisplay "Textdisplay") using [textDisplayAddText](/wiki/TextDisplayAddText "TextDisplayAddText"). Each text item can be added to multiple displays, if need be.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: A string of text you want to display

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: A floating point number between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating how far down the screen the text should be shown, as a percentage of the height, from the top.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: How important it is that this text should be up to date on client's screens. Valid values are: "low", "medium", "high" which are aliases for 0, 1 and 2 respectively.

parameters.name: red
parameters.description: A value between 0 and 255 indicating how red the text should be.

parameters.name: green
parameters.description: A value between 0 and 255 indicating how green the text should be.

parameters.name: blue
parameters.description: A value between 0 and 255 indicating how blue the text should be.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: A value between 0 and 255 indicating how transparent the text should be, with 0 being fully transparent, and 255 being opaque.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: A floating point value indicating the scale of the text. The default is 1.0, which is around 12pt.

parameters.name: alignX
parameters.description: A string representing the X-alignment of the text. ("left", "center", "right")

parameters.name: alignY
parameters.description: A string representing the Y-alignment of the text. ("top", "center", "bottom")

parameters.name: shadowAlpha
parameters.description: A value between 0 and 255 indicating how dark the drop shadow should be.

returns.name: value
returns.description: Returns a textitem object.

contracts.description:
This function triggers an event previously registered on a client.
This is the primary means of passing information between the server and the client.
Clients have a similar [[triggerServerEvent]] function that can do the reverse. You can treat this function as if it was an
asynchronous function call, using [[triggerServerEvent]] to pass back any returned information if necessary.

parameters.name: sendTo
parameters.description: The event will be sent to all [players](/reference/player "Player") that are children of the specified element. By default this is the [root](/reference/root "Root") element, and hence the event is sent to all players. If you specify a single player it will just be sent to that player. This argument can also be a table of player elements.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the event to trigger client side. You should register this event with [[addEvent]] and add at least one event handler using [[addEventHandler]].

parameters.name: sourceElement
parameters.description: The element that is the [source](/reference/Event_System "Event System") of the event.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: A list of arguments to trigger with the event. You can pass any lua data type (except functions). You can also pass [elements](/reference/Element "Element").

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the event trigger has been sent, otherwise **false** if invalid arguments were specified.

contracts.description:
This function will trigger a named [event](/reference/Event_System "Event") on a specific [[element]] in the [element tree](/reference/Element_tree "Element tree"). See [event system](/reference/Event_System "Event System") for more information on how the event system works.
You can use the value returned from this function to determine if the event was cancelled by one of the event handlers. You should determine what your response (if any) to this should be based on the event's purpose. Generally, cancelling an event should prevent any further code being run that is dependent on whatever triggered that event. For example, if you have an `onFlagCapture` event, cancelling it would be expected to prevent the flag being able to be captured. Similarly, if you have `onPlayerKill` as an event you trigger, canceling it would either be expected to prevent the player being killed from dying or at least prevent the player from getting a score for it.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The name of the event you wish to trigger.

parameters.name: baseElement
parameters.description: The element you wish to trigger the event on. See [event system](/reference/Event_System "Event System") for information on how this works.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: The first argument that the event handler expects should be added after the baseElement variable. NOTE: This function can have more than one of these arguments specified, once for each argument the event handler is expecting.

returns.name: result
returns.description: Returns **true** if the event was triggered successfully, otherwise **false** if the event was cancelled using [[cancelEvent]], or **nil** if the arguments are invalid or the event could not be found.

contracts.description: Pre-flight check that reports whether two peds can form a native GTA couple and which one should lead.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: First candidate ped simulated by this client.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Second candidate ped simulated by this client.

contracts.returnDescription: A table with compatible, aLeader, leaderIndex, walkSpeedA and walkSpeedB; false without resource context or when the pair cannot be evaluated.
notes: Leadership is derived from the two native walk speeds. A pair with incompatible speeds would immediately exceed its own give-up distance.
Pass the returned leaderIndex straight into acquirePedNativeCouple; that is the intended flow.
This creates nothing and leases nothing.
contracts.example:
local check = validatePedNativeCouple(pedA, pedB)
if check and check.compatible then
    local token = acquirePedNativeCouple(pedA, pedB, check.leaderIndex)
end

contracts.description: This function copies all contents of a certain node in a XML document to a new document file, so the copied node becomes the new file's root node. The new file will not be saved to file system until [xmlSaveFile](/xmlSaveFile) is called.

If the file is to be in the current resource, only the file path is necessary, e.g. `"newfile.xml"`.

sourceElement.description: The source of this event is the root element.
